info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package lsp is live semantic code intelligence — definitions, references, types, hover, outline and diagnostics — over a repository AND its resolved dependencies, with no toolchain on the caller's machine.

post.summary: Offers the candidates a language server has at a position, typed and resolved through the repository's dependencies rather than guessed from text.
post.description:
Offers the candidates a language server has at a position, typed and
resolved through the repository's dependencies rather than guessed from text.

post.summary: Reports every problem the language server finds in one file — compile errors, type errors and lints, each with its span and its severity (1 error, 2 warning, 3 information, 4 hint).
post.description:
Reports every problem the language server finds in one file —
compile errors, type errors and lints, each with its span and its severity (1
error, 2 warning, 3 information, 4 hint). The position is ignored.

post.summary: Renders the type and documentation of the symbol at a position, as the language server itself renders it.
post.description:
Renders the type and documentation of the symbol at a position, as the
language server itself renders it.

Positions are the LSP's: line and character are 0-BASED and character counts
UTF-16 code units, so an editor's 1-based line must have 1 subtracted before it
is sent. The repository is named by slug and is always one in the caller's own
org; rev pins a branch, tag or commit sha, and empty means the default branch.

post.summary: Finds where a symbol lives: its definition, its references, its type or its implementations, chosen by relation (definition, reference, type, implementation — empty means definition).
post.description:
Finds where a symbol lives: its definition, its references, its type or
its implementations, chosen by relation (definition, reference, type,
implementation — empty means definition).

It resolves THROUGH dependencies. An answer whose external flag is set left the
repository, and its path is then the module coordinate it landed in — which is
the question a static index cannot answer and this service exists for.

post.summary: Outlines one file: every declaration in it, with its kind and its span.
post.description:
Outlines one file: every declaration in it, with its kind and its span.
The position is ignored — the answer is the whole file.

cold.description:
Cold reports that this request paid to PREPARE the revision — the tree
write, the dependency fetch and the language server's first index. It is
the billed event, surfaced so a caller can see what it was charged for.

completions.description:
Completions is complete's answer: the candidates at the position, typed and
resolved through the repository's dependencies rather than guessed from text.

diagnostics.description:
Diagnostics is diagnostics' answer: every problem the server finds in the
whole file, position ignored. Empty means it found none.

hover.description:
Hover is hover's answer: the type and documentation as the language server
itself renders them, so it is prose meant to be shown, not parsed.

lang.description:
Lang is the language the server that answered speaks ("go"), as the daemon
reports it. Empty when the daemon named none.

locations.description:
Locations is locate's answer: where the symbol is defined, referenced, typed
or implemented, per the relation asked for. Empty means the server resolved
nothing there, which is an answer.

op.description:
Op is the question that was asked: hover, locate, symbols, diagnostics or
complete. It names which result field below is the populated one.

path.description: Path is the repo-relative file the question was about, echoed back.

repo.description: Repo is the repository the question was about, echoed back.

rev.description:
Rev is the RESOLVED commit sha, never the branch or tag that was asked for.
It is what makes an answer re-askable: a branch moves, this does not.

symbols.description: Symbols is symbols' answer: the file's whole outline, position ignored.

detail.description: Detail is the server's short elaboration, typically the type or signature.

kind.description:
Kind is the LSP CompletionItemKind number (2 method, 3 function, 5 field, 6
variable, …), passed through as the protocol spells it.

label.description: Label is the text a client would insert, and what an editor lists.

code.description:
Code is the checker's own identifier for the rule, a string or a number
depending on the server. Absent when it published none.

message.description: Message is the problem in the server's own words, meant to be shown.

range.description: Range is the span the problem is about.

severity.description:
Severity is the LSP's: 1 error, 2 warning, 3 information, 4 hint. A file with
only 3s and 4s still compiles.

source.description:
Source is which checker reported it ("compiler", "go vet", a linter's name),
which is what separates a build error from a style opinion.

external.description:
External is true when the answer left the repository — the case a static index
cannot answer, and the reason this service resolves through dependencies.

path.description:
Path is repo-relative while External is false, and the module coordinate
("golang.org/x/mod@v0.14.0/semver/semver.go") once it is true.

range.description: Range is the span inside that file, in LSP positions.

character.description:
Character is a 0-based UTF-16 code-unit offset within Line, per the LSP
specification: not a byte offset and not a rune index. An emoji before the
cursor counts as one here and as two in Go's arithmetic.

line.description:
Line is 0-BASED, per the LSP specification — one less than the line an editor
shows a human.

character.description:
Character is a 0-based UTF-16 code-unit offset within Line, per the LSP
specification — not a byte offset and not a rune index.

line.description: Line is 0-based, per the LSP specification.

path.description: Path is the repo-relative file, e.g. "apps/lsp/lsp.go".

relation.description:
Relation refines locate: definition, reference, type or implementation.
Empty means definition. Every other op ignores it.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository NAME within the caller's own org, e.g. "cloud".
Not a URL and not an owner/name pair: the owner is the validated
principal's org, so this names a repository the caller already owns.

rev.description:
Rev is a branch, tag or commit sha. Empty means the default branch. It is
resolved to a commit before anything else happens, so an answer is always
about one immutable tree.

end.description:
End is the position just past the span, excluded — the range is half-open, so
an empty range has Start equal to End.

start.description: Start is the first position in the span, included.

detail.description:
Detail is the server's short elaboration, typically the signature. Absent when
it offered none.

kind.description:
Kind is the LSP SymbolKind number (5 class, 6 method, 12 function, 23 struct,
…), passed through rather than translated to a word — these callers already
speak LSP, and inventing a second vocabulary is how the two drift.

range.description: Range is the declaration's span in the file.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
